key_insight: A self-learning GNN clustering loop can repeatedly refine node embeddings and graph structure to better exploit both edges and node attributes in fully unsupervised graph clustering.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical template for improving clustering on attributed networks where either topology or features alone are weak signals, including in real-world knowledge-mining and graph analytics pipelines.
method: Run a GNN to learn node representations from the current graph.
Cluster the embeddings and use the clustering result to update the graph for the next round.
Use a context graph derived from the original graph in every round to guide representation learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gains on synthetic data when both network and attributes are weak, and competitive performance on real datasets, especially when clusters are balanced.
watch_item: Performance may drop when cluster sizes are highly imbalanced, and the iterative self-learning loop adds implementation and convergence complexity.
paper_title: Clustering Node Attributed Networks with Graph Neural Networks and Self Learning
